next_state_election.name: State and Federal General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Election Calendar

glance_notes.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — How to Register to Vote
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Tennessee's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5. Tennessee requires registration at least 30 days before an election, with the deadline adjusted when necessary under state law.

glance_notes.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Early Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Early Voting: Registered Tennessee voters may vote early in person without providing a reason. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the statewide early-voting period runs from October 14 through October 29. Locations and daily hours are established by county election commissions.

glance_notes.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: Absentee by Mail Requires Eligibility: Tennessee does not provide no-excuse absentee voting by mail. A voter must meet one of the qualifying reasons established by state law. A completed absentee ballot must be returned by mail or an authorized commercial carrier and received by the county election commission by the close of polls on Election Day.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Tennessee residents may register online, by mail or in person. Online registration is available to eligible applicants with a Tennessee driver's license or Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security identification card. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be a Tennessee resident and be at least 18 years old on or before Election Day. A person convicted of a felony may be ineligible unless voting rights have been restored under Tennessee law. A submitted registration application does not make a person registered until the county election commission processes and accepts the application.
register.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — How to Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Tennessee's felony voting-rights rules are unusually complex and have changed through litigation and administrative policy. Do not summarize them as automatic restoration after release, probation or sentence completion. Direct affected voters to the Secretary of State's current Restoration of Voting Rights guidance and county election officials.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Tennessee's GoVoteTN system to check voter registration information and obtain voter-specific election information. GoVoteTN provides polling locations, sample ballots, elected-official information and other voting information based on the voter's registration or residential address. Questions about the accuracy of a voter record should be directed to the appropriate county election commission.
check_registration.internal_note: GoVoteTN is the official statewide voter-information application. Its data is supplied by local county election commissions and includes sample ballots and polling locations.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Tennessee requires eligible voters to register before the statutory registration deadline rather than offering general Election Day registration. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the voter registration deadline is Monday, October 5. Online applications must be submitted by the applicable deadline. Mailed registration forms must satisfy Tennessee's deadline requirements, and voters registering close to the deadline should confirm that their registration has been processed before voting.
deadlines.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — How to Register to Vote
deadlines.internal_note: November 3, 2026 is confirmed as Tennessee's state and federal General Election date. Tennessee's ordinary registration cutoff is 30 days before an election. Because the 30th day before November 3 falls on Sunday, October 4, the operative 2026 deadline is Monday, October 5. Tennessee does not provide general same-day registration.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use GoVoteTN to find your Election Day polling location and early-voting locations. Election Day voters generally vote at the polling place assigned to their registered address unless their county provides an authorized vote-center arrangement. Early voting locations are separate, and registered county residents may use the early-voting sites made available by their county election commission. Polling locations can change, so voters should check GoVoteTN shortly before voting.
polling_place.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — GoVoteTN Polling Locations
polling_place.internal_note: GoVoteTN separately identifies Election Day and early-voting locations. Its Election Day interface notes that where multiple authorized locations are displayed, the voter may vote at any listed location. Do not universally tell every Tennessee voter that only one precinct location is permitted because county vote-center arrangements can differ.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Tennessee's State and Federal General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls close at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time and 7:00 p.m. Central Time. Opening times are established by county election commissions within requirements of state law and can vary by county, so voters should use GoVoteTN to confirm their specific polling-place hours. Voters who vote in person generally must present an acceptable federal or Tennessee government-issued photo ID unless an exemption applies.
election_day.glance_value: Polls close 8:00 p.m. ET / 7:00 p.m. CT; check local opening time
election_day.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — GoVoteTN Polling Locations
election_day.internal_note: Tennessee should NOT be given a fabricated uniform statewide opening time. State law requires polls to remain open for specified periods but county election commissions establish opening hours. Statewide closing is synchronized at 8:00 p.m. Eastern / 7:00 p.m. Central. Voters should verify county-specific hours through GoVoteTN.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Tennessee polling-place opening times vary by county. Polls close statewide at the same moment: 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time and 7:00 p.m. Central Time. Voters should use GoVoteTN or contact their county election commission to confirm the opening time and exact hours for their assigned Election Day location.
polling_hours.glance_value: Closing: 8:00 p.m. ET / 7:00 p.m. CT; opening varies
polling_hours.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — GoVoteTN Polling Locations
polling_hours.internal_note: Tennessee spans Eastern and Central time zones. Avoid converting the statewide closing rule into 8:00 p.m. local time everywhere. The equivalent closing times are 8:00 p.m. Eastern and 7:00 p.m. Central. County-specific opening times should be retrieved from GoVoteTN.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Any registered Tennessee voter may vote early in person without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins Wednesday, October 14 and ends Thursday, October 29. Early-voting locations and daily schedules are established by county election commissions, so voters should use GoVoteTN or their county election commission's official information for exact sites and hours. Voters who vote early generally must present the same qualifying photo identification required for Election Day voting.
early_voting.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Early Voting
early_voting.internal_note: Tennessee provides no-excuse early voting. Do not invent uniform statewide daily hours because county schedules vary. Tennessee legislation introduced in 2026 proposed shortening the early-voting period, but a proposal as introduced is not evidence that the law changed. The applicable 2026 General Election schedule remains October 14-29 unless the Secretary of State issues revised official guidance.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Tennessee requires most voters requesting an absentee ballot by mail to meet one of the qualifying reasons established by state law. Qualifying categories include certain voters age 60 or older, voters who will be outside their county during the early-voting period and all of Election Day, voters with qualifying illness, physical disability, hospitalization or caregiving circumstances, certain students and their spouses, qualifying election workers and other categories specified by law. A request generally must be received by the county election commission no later than seven days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, that deadline is October 27. Completed absentee ballots must be returned by mail or an authorized commercial carrier and received by the county election commission no later than the close of polls on Election Day. Tennessee does not permit ordinary absentee ballots to be hand-delivered to the election commission or turned in at a polling place.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Excuse required; request by October 27; ballot due Election Day
absentee_mail.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: Tennessee's absentee system is excuse-based. Age 60 or older is one statutory category. The application deadline is seven days before Election Day, making October 27 the November 2026 deadline. The ballot must actually be received by close of polls; an Election Day postmark is insufficient. Current Secretary of State guidance explicitly says hand delivery is not permitted and return must be by mail, including USPS, FedEx, UPS or another qualifying carrier.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Tennessee voters generally must present photo identification issued by the Tennessee state government or the federal government when voting in person during early voting or on Election Day. Qualifying identification may be current or expired. Examples include a Tennessee driver's license with a photo, Tennessee photo identification card, U.S. passport, U.S. military photo identification and qualifying Tennessee handgun carry permits with a photo. College student identification cards are not accepted. Tennessee law provides exemptions and special procedures for certain voters, including voters who are indigent and unable to obtain acceptable identification without paying a fee.
voter_id.glance_value: Federal or Tennessee government photo ID generally required
voter_id.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.internal_note: The Secretary of State explicitly states that acceptable IDs may be expired. College student IDs are specifically not accepted. Do not imply that every government-issued ID qualifies: the core rule is photo identification issued by the Tennessee state government or federal government, subject to statutory details and exemptions. A free photo ID for voting purposes may be available through the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Tennessee provides accessible voting equipment and assistance for voters with disabilities. A voter who needs assistance because of blindness, disability or inability to read or write may receive assistance at the polling place under Tennessee law. Federal accessibility requirements also apply to polling locations and voting systems. Voters who need specific accommodations should contact their county election commission before voting so available accessibility arrangements and equipment can be confirmed. Some voters with qualifying disabilities may also be eligible to vote absentee by mail.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance and absentee options available
accessible_voting.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Division of Elections
accessible_voting.internal_note: Tennessee counties administer polling-place accessibility and voting equipment locally under state and federal requirements. Because specific equipment and accessibility arrangements can vary, direct voters needing accommodations to their county election commission rather than promising a particular machine at every location.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Tennessee provides special absentee-voting procedures for eligible military personnel, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas under UOCAVA. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot. Tennessee allows qualifying military and overseas voters to receive absentee ballots by email or by mail upon request. Tennessee does not provide ballot delivery by fax. A completed voted ballot must be physically returned and received by the voter's county election commission no later than the close of polls on Election Day. UOCAVA voters may also use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot when eligible.
military_overseas.glance_value: Email or mail ballot delivery; voted ballot due by close of polls
military_overseas.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly confirms that UOCAVA voters may receive ballots by email or mail, but not by fax. The voted ballot must reach the local county election commission by the close of polls on Election Day. Do not imply that electronic ballot delivery permits electronic return of the voted ballot.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Tennessee if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. Students should register using the Tennessee residence they consider their legal voting residence and may vote in only one jurisdiction in an election. A Tennessee student who remains registered in another county and will be outside that county during the entire early-voting period and all of Election Day may qualify to vote absentee by mail. Full-time students attending an accredited college or university outside their county of registration, and qualifying spouses, are among Tennessee's absentee-voting categories. A college student ID is not an acceptable form of photo identification for voting in person in Tennessee.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may qualify for absentee voting; student ID not accepted
student_voting.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
student_voting.internal_note: Tennessee's absentee law includes qualifying full-time students attending accredited colleges or universities outside their county of registration and their spouses. The Secretary of State's voter-ID guidance explicitly states that college student IDs are not accepted for in-person voting. Avoid claiming that merely attending a Tennessee college automatically establishes Tennessee voting residency.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Tennessee voters can use GoVoteTN to view the sample ballot associated with their voter registration or residential address when it is available. Because ballot contents vary by county, district and local contests, voters should use their own information to retrieve the ballot that applies to them. GoVoteTN also provides polling locations and other voter-specific election information.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your sample ballot through GoVoteTN
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official GoVoteTN application explicitly provides sample ballots based on voter information or residential address. Reverify after November 2026 ballots are finalized because contests vary by jurisdiction.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Tennessee Secretary of State, Division of Elections, 312 Rosa L. Parks Avenue, 7th Floor, Nashville, TN 37243. Toll-free voter assistance: 1-877-850-4959. Phone: 615-741-7956. For questions about a specific voter registration record, polling location, absentee ballot or local election procedure, contact the voter's county election commission.
contact.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State — Division of Elections
contact.internal_note: GoVoteTN's current help system directs voters with general voting questions to the Division of Elections at 1-877-850-4959 and provides county-specific election commission contacts for registration questions. No unverified email address was inserted. All reader-facing contact information is plain text.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Tennessee Secretary of State Division of Elections and GoVoteTN for official election information. These resources provide voter registration, voter-specific election information, polling locations, early-voting locations, sample ballots, absentee-voting guidance, voter identification requirements and military and overseas voting information. Tennessee's 95 county election commissions maintain local voter records and administer polling places, early-voting locations, absentee ballots and other county election functions.
